subject: AuroraPoint private install: cluster provisioning and thin-PV contract
messages:
From: SiteCore Ops <ops@sitecore.com>
To: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Sep 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AuroraPoint private cluster - initial scope and timeline

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this on. We're starting procurement for the AuroraPoint site (Tier-2 data center, regional retail campus). Key points from our side:
- Expected steady-state: 2k QPS (burst to 6k) for inference requests, mostly short text gen (avg seq 128).
- Dataset retention: logs persist 30d; model KV caches ephemeral.
- Storage: two NVMe local nodes per rack planned; intent is to use thin-provisioned PVs for workspace artifacts.
- Networking: single 10Gb LAG to customer aggregation switch; private VPC with dedicated egress via our peering.

Can Redwood send a preflight checklist plus guidance on node pool split, recommended PV classes (CSI + encryption), and any contract language we should expect for thin-provisioned blockstore? We'd like a delivery window week of Oct 21.

Paul Hutchins
SiteCore Systems - Infrastructure
ops@sitecore.com

From: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Paul Hutchins <paul.hutchins@sitecore.com>
Cc: SiteCore Ops <ops@sitecore.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Sep 2029 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AuroraPoint private cluster - initial scope and timeline

Paul — thanks, this gives us enough to start a scoping run. Attached: a preliminary preflight checklist (aurorapoint-preflight-checklist.xlsx) with required items for rack power, uplink, KMS certificates, and service-account onboarding.

Quick clarifying Qs:
1) Do you plan to have a separate management VLAN for the control plane (we recommend it)?
2) Is the 10Gb LAG redundant to two top-of-rack switches or a single switch?
3) Will audit logs be forwarded to your SIEM (if yes, which retention tier)?

Initial recommendations in short:
- Node pools: 3 pools — control (3x m4-small), app (6x m8-highmem), io-heavy (2x nvme-io nodes). We'll sketch exact vCPU/RAM after you confirm workloads.
- Storage: recommend CSI LVM + thin provisioning for ephemeral workspaces, and an encrypted blockstore class (CSI) for anything needing persistence.
- Encryption: KMS with customer-managed keys; bring-your-own (we support AWS KMS-like API or HSM-backed wrapped keys).

I'll loop in Karthik for sizing and Marissa for delivery milestones; new items will go into DEP-1293.

Best,
Irene Choi\Head of Private Deployments\Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Sep 2029 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: AuroraPoint: need nodepool & PV recommendations (see external thread)

Karthik / Marissa,

Forwarding Paul’s scope below. They want thin-provisioned PVs for workspace artifacts and an encrypted blockstore for persistent data, and are aiming for an Oct 21 window. Questions for you:
- Karthik: given 2k steady QPS, bursts to 6k, mostly short seqs, what app-node shape would you propose (cpu/mem), and what target pod density should we plan for? Also guidance on eviction thresholds and ephemeral PV sizes.
- Marissa: can you confirm delivery SLAs and what tasks we must schedule to meet an Oct 21 onboard (in particular, rack-level on-site acceptance and runbook handoff)?

I attached the checklist I sent. Please reply with concrete numbers / task list by EOD Fri so I can return to the customer.

Thanks,
Irene

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Sep 2029 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AuroraPoint: need nodepool & PV recommendations (see external thread)

Irene — notes below; I referenced the checklist and the workload profile.

SIZING PROPOSAL (initial)
- Control plane: 3x m4.small (2 cores, 8GB); control-plane taints + static reservations (kubeadm-managed).
- App pool: 8x m8-highmem (16 cores, 128GB) — plan for 50 pods/node average; target request ratio 0.4 CPU / pod, 1.5GB RAM / pod. This yields ~400 pods capacity for the app pool to absorb 2k steady. We'll tune after load test.
- IO pool (local NVMe): 3x nvme-io nodes (24 cores, 192GB, 4 x 3.2TB NVMe) — nodes dedicated to heavy ephemeral workspaces and any KV-local caches. Use nodeAffinity + taints so only IO workloads land here.

STORAGE CLASSES
- csi-lvm-thin (recommended for ephemeral workspaces): LVM thin pools on NVMe, dynamic provisioning via our CSI plugin. Default reclaim: Delete.
- csi-encrypted-block (for persistent artifacts): iSCSI/Ceph/RBD backed with server-side encryption; encryption-at-rest using customer-managed key. Reclaim: Retain, unless customer requests otherwise.

THIN-PV CONTRACT NOTE (legal flag)
- Thin provisioning requires explicit overcommit language in contract (we need to specify dedup/overprovision behavior, expected oversubscription ratio (recommend max 3:1 for NVMe thin-pools), and a remediation SLA if shared thin pools reach critical pressure). I suggest Redwood propose the 3:1 guidance and the following remediation sequence: throttling admissions -> emergency autoscale -> manual offload.

NETWORK / SLOS
- Recommend separate mgmt VLAN for control plane and an egress VLAN for inference traffic. Use BGP peering to the customer's aggregation switch; request two top-of-rack switches for redundancy.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 180ms for short seqs; we assume local NVMe will keep warm-cold transitions low.

OPERATIONAL GUARDS
- Eviction thresholds: soft at 70% disk usage, hard at 85%.
- Monitoring: node-level NVMe SMART + CSI pool utilization exported to Prometheus with alerts at 60/75/85%.
- Backup: persistent volume snapshots nightly for blockstore; ephemeral thin-pv not snapshotted by default.

I'll draft a short technical appendix for the contract (oversubscription ratios, metric triggers) and drop into DEP-1293. Marissa - can you own the contract/SLAs and the delivery milestone table?

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Paul Hutchins <paul.hutchins@sitecore.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Sep 2029 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AuroraPoint private cluster - initial scope and timeline

Paul — thanks for the patience. Attached is the preflight checklist and the initial PV/oversubscription appendix. Highlights:
- Proposed node pools: control (3), app (8), io-nvme (3) — exact shapes are in the checklist.
- Storage classes: csi-lvm-thin (default ephemeral), csi-encrypted-block (retain, CMK).
- Contract language: we propose a maximum oversubscription of 3:1 for NVMe thin pools with the remediation path (throttle -> autoscale -> manual offload).

Next steps:
1) Review the attached PV IO contract (aurorapoint-pv-io-contract-v1.pdf). If acceptable, please sign via the DocuSign link below by Sep 24 so we can reserve the Oct 21 window.
2) Confirm top-of-rack redundancy (one switch vs two) and whether logs go to your SIEM.
3) We'll run a preflight remote health-check 72 hours before rack install.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/aurorapoint/SC-AUR-2029-09
Jira: DEP-1293

Best regards,
Irene Choi\Head of Private Deployments\Redwood Inference
